TRAINING: Thai boxing in the morning, BJJ training in the afternoon.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started my sports career as a track and field athlete, and then I started to train Sanda. My Sanda coaches found me to have good talents in fighting and they introduced / sent me to the Xian Sports University, which is one of the cradles of fighting in China.

What ranks and titles have you held? None

Do you have any heroes? GSP is my hero.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? The UFC is the world's no.1 MMA promotion. If I can finally get the chance to fight for the UFC, it means to me that I became one of the best fighters in the world.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I studied and trained at Xian Sports University, but I don't yet have a degree.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was a student.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I've won some fights in the amateur BJJ competitions in China.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Blue belt in BJJ

Favorite grappling technique: Armbar

Favorite striking technique: Sanda punches

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I started traditional Chinese martial arts training when I was 12. After two years I started to train Sanda and joined the Shanxi province Sanda team.  When I was 16, I had my first pro MMA fight, but I wasn’t good at grappling at that time. Then I started my official MMA training at 17 years old.

What ranks and titles have you held? 2018 MMA World Cup Junior Champion, Shan Xi province Sanda Champion

Do you have any heroes? Roy Jones Jr, Badr Hari, Anderson Silva

What would it mean for you to fight in the UFC? If I am a teenager, I would say my dream becomes true. But now, I would like to say this is my first step; if I fight in UFC this will be the new start of my life and my career.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Shandong Sport University - English major

Ranks in any martial arts styles: BJJ blue belt

Favorite grappling technique: RNC

Favorite Striking technique: Side kick

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I have been a Sanda athlete and have been training in Sanda until I found MMA. MMA rules really made my dreams possible, and at that moment, I said to myself, “UFC, I am coming.”

Training: 6k run in the morning and then standup technique training. Jiu-jitsu, physical conditioning, wrestling, MMA at night.

What ranks and titles have you held? Two-time UFC strawweight champion

Do you have any heroes? My father

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It is a dream realized and a new beginning. This is a step closer to my goal. I still remember that on February 23, 2013, UFC 157’s main event was with Ronda Rousey and Liz Carmouche. This was the battle that showed that the world’s largest fighting organization was officially open to women. Since then, I hoped that I could stand here and become the best among them and realize the ultimate dream in every athlete’s heart – the gold championship belt.

What was your job before you started fighting? Sanda athlete, fitness instructor

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Brown belt in jiu-jitsu

qna.value:
What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC? It means I can compete against the best fighters in the world, and it also brings me one step closer to my goal. 

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training Sanda in 2010. Later I also trained in kickboxing and Mua Thai before eventually transitioning to MMA. I’ve been seriously training MMA for around four years. I started fighting because I’m naturally competitive and I love the feeling of winning. 

What are your current ranks in martial arts?

  • National Kickboxing Champion
  • National Muay Thai Champion
  • National Sanda Champion
  • China National First-Class Athlete

Specific accomplishments in pro competition?

  • Champion and belt holder of the National Professional Kickboxing League
  • Champion and belt holder of the National Professional Muay Thai League
  • National University Sanda Games Champion 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Graduated from Guangzhou Sport University with a Bachelor’s Degree

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked as a Sanda coach

Favorite grappling technique: None. I really hate grappling.

Favorite striking technique: Heavy punches and powerful kicks

Tell us about your life outside of fighting:No wife, no kids, no girlfriend, and no pets. In my free time, I enjoy being alone or hanging out with friends, eating and drinking together.

Fighter Facts

  • Pro since 2011
     
  • Nine wins by submission (3 RNC, leg lock, 4 arm lock, triangle choke)
     
  • Five first-round finishes
     
  • Owns 2020 submission win over TUF / DWCS vet Ricky Steele

 

UFC History

UFC Fight Night (10/23/21) Lazishvili lost a three-round unanimous decision to Jonathan Martinez

 

Q&A

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training quite late at the age of 19. Counting my active phases of training, it will be around eight years now.  My father was a freestyle wrestler, but he never wanted me to be an athlete; instead he would push me to study and find a different profession in this life. The way I started my professional training was not that fun. During a street fight in my hometown (In Caucasus at that time in Georgia you had to fight if it was needed. Sometimes it was quite wild because we would meet 20-40 boys against each other; it was our kind of entertainment) my future couch Koba Tkeshelashvili noticed me and after some time he found me and offered me to train with him in the capital city. I was around 19 at that time so it was the year I started my university in Tbilisi so, I went to him and after that day he would try his best to make me come to train even when I was missing class; he would come pick me up and bring me to a cage. Now I`m very grateful for that.
What ranks and titles have you held? Kombat League world champion in MMA (145 pounds), Kombat League World champion in Grappling (155pounds), Georgian champion in Grappling (3 different weight divisions), LFA bantamweight Champion
Do you have any heroes? My Father
What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? For the boy who came from my background, training on a rough cement floor breaking the knees without having any inventory, training in an empty room with broken windows in winter cold or crazy hot summer days without even knowing what MMA is...it was my goal to get to UFC. I knew where I was going; it was my ultimate destination. Moreover, I will get that belt sooner or later.
Did you go to college and if so, what degree did you earn? I did my bachelor’s back in Tbilisi in Business Administration. In the U.S. I came with 100% scholarship, and I got a master’s degree in Business Administration, then I got my 80% scholarship and finished a second master’s in Data Analytics.  I like learning a new stuff; it extends your perception.
What was your job before you started fighting? Back in Georgia I used to work for a stock market company. I was in sales, then I moved to Russia, where I had my own business in Moscow, a retail company. Here, I also have some good commercial ideas after my documents will be done, and hopefully I will fulfill them.

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? When I was a kid, I opened the door of the judo club when I was nine years old. My parents got divorced and I did not see any other choice who could show for me a better example like my coaches Tomas Putinauskas and Arturas Sakas

What professional titles have you held? MMA Bushido title 

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Silver medalist in world combat sambo championship in Tashkent

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Judo blue belt, European grappling champion 

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? My first fight in TUF 32. I got knocked down, and stood up from there, got inspired on the inside and won that fight.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Valentina Shevchenko, because she is a unique person

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I have a bachelor’s degree from Vytautas Magnus University. I’m a teacher 

What was your job before you started fighting? I’m still working in the Lithuanian military and as a teacher 

Personal Life/Background: Riding my motorbike, shooting guns, fishing, hiking in the mountains.
